#1370. In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1,2,3,4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5,6,7,8,9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

a, Quantification of CD3− cells 5 days after CRISPR-mediated gene editing in three independent donors. b, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing with the indicated Cas9 mRNA concentrations, n = 3 biologically independent replicates. Data are shown as mean + s.e.m. Significance was calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test. ns, not significant. c, Left, representative flow cytometry plots showing CD3 and CD28 protein-level DKO efficiency in activated human primary T cells 5 days after Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Right, quantification of CD3+ CD28+ cells in DKO and vector control groups; data are shown as mean + s.e.m.; n = 4 infection replicates. Significance was calculated using a paired two-sided t-test, ****P < 0.0001. d, Quantification of CD3− or CD28− cells 5 days after editing; n = 3 donors per concentration. Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. e, Classification and composition of targeted genes in the T cell DKO CRISPR library. f, Schematic of the two-step T cell DKO CRISPR library construction process. g, Quantification of plasmid library sgRNA-pair construct distribution. h, Flow cytometry histograms showing EGFRvIII expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. i, Flow cytometry histograms showing PD-L1 expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. j, Schematic of DKO CAR-T cell library generation pipeline, including human T cell isolation and activation, CAR-T cell generation and selection, lentiviral DKO CRISPR library infection and Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Schematic in panel j created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/4g9xapi (2026). k, Spider plots of tumour volumes for donor 1 in vivo screen experiment shown in Fig. 1d. n = 5 biologically independent mice. l, Representative H&E-stained tumour sections from two biologically independent tumours per group from the screen shown in Fig. 1c. Scale bar, 250 μm. m, sgRNA-pair detection rates from the total library across individual samples. D, donor; T, tumour. n, Heat map of Spearman correlation coefficients between the log2-normalized counts-per-million (log-norm.) sgRNA counts for each sample. Data were arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method. o, Multidimensional scaling analysis of log2-normalized screen data using the top 10,000 most variable sgRNA pairs across samples. Data points were clustered by k-means. p, Box-dot plot of library representation across individual samples, showing the distribution of all sgRNA-pair constructs counts. Boxes indicate the 25th–75th percentiles, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range. Individual points represent sgRNA-pair counts. q, Empirical cumulative distribution function of DKO library representation among detected sgRNA pairs in plasmid, pre-injection cell and tumour samples. Sample labels in m-p indicate sample type, plasmid, pre-injection cell or tumour, and donor ID.

a, Distribution of the top four performing sgRNA-pair constructs for top DKO hits across samples, ranked by SAMBA sgRNA z-score. b, Heat map of DKO screen scores for all pairwise gene combinations assessed in the CRISPR screen. Values were scaled and visualized within a range of −1 to 1. Hierarchical clustering was performed using the Ward.D2 method based on Euclidean distances. c, Scatter plot showing the relationship between screen enrichment and synergistic effect. SAMBA z-scores were plotted against synergy scores for each gene pair. Dashed lines indicate FDR-adjusted P value, q < 0.05, for epistasis and SAMBA results. d, Scatter plot of observed DKO SAMBA scores versus expected SAMBA scores based on the additive effects of the corresponding SKOs for each gene pair (SKO1 + SKO2). Points are colored by synergy score. Linear regression yielded R2 = 0.0152 (n = 2,485 gene pairs; 71 SKO genes), indicating minimal predictability of DKO outcomes from SKO additivity. e, Quantification of indel frequencies in DKO-edited CAR-T cells 5 days after electroporation across three independent batches. P values were calculated using unpaired two-sided t-tests. Data are mean ± s.e.m.; n = 3 human donors. Each dot represents one human donor. f, Quantification of indel frequencies in CAR-T cells from three donors generated across three independent batches 90 days after gene editing. P values were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC. Data are mean + s.e.m.; n = 3 independent donor-derived CAR-T cell preparations, generated from three donors in independent batches. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing in different DKO CAR-T cells compared with controls, n = 3 infection replicates per group. b, Schematic of generation of DKO CAR-T or CAR-Jurkat cell generation and downstream assays. Schematic in panel b created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/7vyyd1r (2026). c, Quantification of Ca2+ flux AUC and peak signal change in different DKO CAR-Jurkat samples. The resting region was defined as 1 min before antigen crosslinking, and the peak region was defined as 500 s after cross-linking. AUC is calculated as (mean peak signal – mean resting signal) × 500. Representative of three independent experiments. d, Quantification of pERK1/2 (pT202/pY204) signal in DKO CAR-Jurkat cells after U87-GL-EGFRvIII stimulation at the indicated time points; n = 3 per group per time point. e, Quantification of pERK1/2+ (pT202/pY204) DKO CAR-T cells after U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell stimulation for 30 min; n = 3 biological replicates per group. f-g, NF-κB CFP and NFAT/AP-1 GFP reporter activity after coculture of U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells with different DKO CD8+ CAR-Jurkat cells with GTC control at indicated time points. E:T = 1:2. n = 3 per group per time point. f, Schematic of the NFAT/AP-1 GFP reporter structure and quantification of GFP+ cells. g, Schematic of the NF-κB CFP reporter structure and the quantification of CFP+ cells. h, Quantifications of tonic signaling in CAR-Jurkat cells after 1 month cell culture without stimulation, n = 3. P value was determined by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s correction for multiple comparisons test versus GTC. i, Left, representative flow cytometry histograms showing CD107a expression in CD8+ DKO and GTC CAR-T cells after 2-h coculture with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells. Right, quantification of CD107a+ CAR-T cells; n = 4 per group; E:T = 1:2. j, Quantification of IFN-γ, TNF, and granzyme B expression in CD8+ and CD4+ CAR-T cells after 4-h coculture with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells at E:T = 1:8; n = 4 per group. k, Left, quantification of CellTrace Violetlow CAR-T cells after two rounds of repeated antigen stimulation, measured on day 5, n = 6 each. Right, quantification of absolute CAR-T cell numbers; n = 3 on day 0, n = 6 on day 2, 5, and 7 per group. l, Quantification of CellTrace Violetlow CAR-T cells in low IL-2 medium, measured on day 7; n = 3 per group. m, Quantification of live cells percentage in culture or after repeated challenge. n, Left, quantification of CD45RO+ CD62L+ DKO CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5. Right, quantification of CD27+ DKO CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 6 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. o, Quantifications of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells after repeated tumour challenge on day 5, n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. p, Quantification of LAG-3+, PD-1+, TIM-3+ CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. q, SPICE analysis of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells on day 5. Data are group means. r, Quantification of absolute CAR-T cell number after IL-2 withdrawal; n = 3 per group at day 0, n = 4 per group at day 2, 5, and 7. Data in d-g,k right,m,r are mean ± s.e.m.; data in a,h-j,k left,l,n-p are mean + s.e.m. Significance levels were calculated using ordinary two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test comparing each group with GTC within each row or time point (d-g,j,k right,m,r), repeated-measures one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC (a), or ordinary one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC (h,i,k left,l,n-p). Dashed lines in c, i, j, n-p indicate mean values of the GTC group. n indicates biologically independent samples unless otherwise stated. Exact P values and detailed statistics are provided in the Source Data. Data are representative of three independent experiments using cells from human donors independent of those used in the screen. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

Data in h-j,l,m are mean ± s.e.m.; data in a-d,n,r-t,v are mean + s.e.m. Significance levels were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC (a-c,s,t), one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (d), ordinary two-way ANOVA with Šídák’s multiple-comparisons test comparing DKO with each indicated control within each antigen-expression condition (h,i), ordinary two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test within each row or condition (j,n), two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Šídák’s multiple-comparisons test comparing DKO with each indicated control at each time point (l,m), or ordinary two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC within each row or condition (r,v). n indicates biologically independent samples unless otherwise stated. #1369. Academy Graduate Tom Davies Features In Under-21s Game

Academy graduate Tom Davies will feature in Everton Under-21s' Premier League 2 clash away to Crystal Palace on Sunday, as the Academy continues to support the midfielder with his fitness as he looks to secure a professional contract elsewhere.

Davies – a free agent after leaving Sheffield United at the end of last season – has been training with the Under-21s to support the Blues' younger players while building his own fitness.

Davies, who will start on the bench this afternoon, joined Everton Academy at the age of 11 and developed through the age groups before making his Men’s debut aged 17 in April 2016.

The boyhood Blue became the youngest captain in Everton’s history when he skippered the side, aged 20, for a 2018 Carabao Cup tie.

#1368. Mary Earps is a mum! Euro-winning Lionesses goalkeeper reveals her partner has secretly given birth to a baby boy - but she won't be able to take maternity leave due to football

Published: 09:53 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 09:53 EDT, 6 November 2026

Euro-winning Lionesses goalkeeper Mary Earps has become a mother for the first time, revealing today that her partner has given birth to a baby boy.

Earps, 33, was a hero of England's Euro 2022 victory at Wembley and starred at the World Cup in 2023, saving a penalty in the final. She won BBC Sports Personality of the Year but later lost her England place to rival Hannah Hampton and retired in acrimonious circumstances.

She moved to France with Paris Saint-Germain but returned to England earlier this year - and has now welcomed her first child with her partner, Kitty Forrest.

In a video released today, Earps said: 'I've been keeping a little secret from you all. And I don't think I can talk my way out of this one. So, I think I'm going to have to show you.

'I can't quite believe I'm writing this, but yesterday Kitty and I welcomed our beautiful baby boy into the world!

'We're absolutely over the moon and still trying to take it all in. It's been such an emotional journey getting to this point, and we couldn't be more excited to start this next chapter of our lives as a family of three.'

Mary Earps and her partner Kitty have revealed news of welcoming a baby boy (YouTube/Mary Earps)

The happy couple shared their news after keeping the pregnancy secret (YouTube/Mary Earps)

Earps says she will not be able to take maternity leave due to the rigors of the football season. Her team, London City Lionesses, are eight games into the new Women's Super League season and sit third behind Chelsea and Manchester City.

'I do have one eye sort of on football, which is super weird,' she said.

'In any other job, you would just be like, "Okay, bye. Taking maternity leave, whatever. Um, and you just do what you need to do." But that doesn't really work in football, because you've got games and then, if you take the day off, then you got to think about what that looks like and how that works into sort of your training schedule and the fixture calendar.

'So, it's a little bit more complicated. You can't just take annual leave whenever you want without consequence. You know, it's going to be interesting to see what the next days and weeks bring.'

Earps first revealed that she was in a same-sex relationship in September of last year but largely kept partner Kitty out of the spotlight.

Kitty is a physiotherapist who worked as the lead in her department at Manchester United Women, Earps's former club.

Earps is pictured kissing the trophy after England won Euro 2022 at Wembley Stadium

Earps won BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2023 following her Euro heroics

In a statement at the time, Earps said: 'I've always tried to keep my personal life separate from my professional one, but it would have felt inauthentic not to include something so important to me in this book. I'm in a really happy relationship.

'The people closest to me have always known, and I feel ready and happy to share that with everyone else now.'

Earps retired from England duty in May last year after the release of her autobiography dragged up a storm with Hampton, the Chelsea goalkeeper who overtook her from understudy to become England No 1.

Earps revealed she told Sarina Wiegman that 'bad behaviour was being rewarded' after Hampton was recalled to the England squad.

#1367. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

[Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he shows a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

"That one was for you, nan" Jack Rudoni explains his goal celebration ❤️ https://t.co/79OvHMlu6J

A victory to savour for Coventry whose teenagers Cherif and Mfuni scored fine goals. No doubt they wobbled when Botman equalised and for the next 10 minutes but Newcastle blew too many chances and resumed making errors at the back. Newcastle’s squad is a mess.

Newcastle might maintain that Thomas-Asante was offside and blocking the keeper’s view when Mfuni pulled the trigger but I think Hornicke had a clear view and hence it wasn’t an offence.

The first two minutes of stoppage time, of which there are four, pass without incident.

Osula lifts a volley over the bar with a wild attempt. Toure was injured in the build-up and will be replaced by Dan Burn.

Never mind Bob Gelodof and Brenda Ann Spencer, Matthias Jaissle doesn’t like Mondays. They are 8-2 down on Monday Night Football so far this season.

Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 (Mfuni) The substitute had only just replaced Rudoni and took the ball on the inside-left 25 yards out, advanced then wrapped his instep around a left-foot shot, arrowing it across Hornicek into the bottom right.

Stephen Mfuni makes his mark for Coventry! 👊 https://t.co/KI2kgpfUJP

Thomas-Asante crashes a right-foot shot into the heart of the left post. A thumping strike that leaves the metalwork ringing.

Coventry 3 Newcastle 1 (Simms) Right foot shot from 18 yards through Thiaw’s legs, clipping the inside of his right knee to deflect it into the bottom left. Joelinton had been trying to dribble it out of the box, overhit it and fouled Thomas-Asante as he tried to recover. The whistle was betweeen the ref’s lips but he did not exhale as Simms steered his shot through Thiaw’s legs.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

Touré beats Dasilva for pace down the right then blazes over from a tight angle then moments later is given an opportunity to shoot and sticks it in the stands again. Both times the cross was on.

Toure has caused untold problems for Dasilva. Newcastle corner on the left is bent far too deep and goes out for a goal-kick.

Wissa dithers over a shot when found by Toure to the right of the penalty spot and finally clips it into Thomas. Coventry are clinging on but flapping. As is the crowd.

Hall, following Botman’s lead, lets fly from distance, straight at Rushworth.

Coventry fluff a couple of chances to break with hasty, panicked passes.

It was as if Coventry were defying him to have a shot. And in doing so, the nerves are back with a bang in the crowd.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 1 (Botman) Coventry invite him to shoot by backing off and backing off and he RSVPs with a left-foot torpedo from 20 yards into the roof of the net. What a strike!

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

Barnes appears to have been brought down by Sakamoto in the Coventry penalty area but he was offside. One of Jaissle’s staff is booked for some verbal transgression.

Joelinto rattles bones in a tackle that was not shown as they focus on Barnes’ spurious penalty appeal when he slipped behind Pinnock.

Rudoni dips his shoulder and skins Botman in the Newcastle box but tries and fails to square it to Cherif instead of shooting.

Touré makes ground down the right and slips Joelinton down the inside. The substitute, who took the captain’s armband off Thiaw, tries to find Pardo with a cross that Thomas blocks.

Now Willock blazes over from eight yards on the right after a slick one-two with Murphy.

Dedic → MileyTouré → MurphyJoelinton → Willock

Rushworth drops Hall’s cross but recovers to grab it on the bounce. Jaissle has three subs stripped. Murphy tries to bend a cross from the right to Barnes at the back post but Van Ewijk and Thomas combine to scramble it out for a throw-in.

Now Cherif misses a gilded opportunity after a hacked clearance from Botman lands at his feet to the left of the spot. He kicks it into his other leg and the ball dribbles wide. The way Botman dealt with Thomas-Asante’s cross was really shoddy.

Barnes disguises his inside run and evades Van Ewijk to collect Thiaw’s pass up the inside-right channel. He spins and feeds it infield to Wissa who telegraphs his shot with a laboured touch before swiinging a right-footer from 25 yards straight down Rushworth’s throat.

Newcastle have been awful. Seem to lack leadership and heft on the field. The return of Joelinton can’t come quick enough.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 0 (Cherif) Talented lad. Absolutely larrups a right-foot shot through a thicket of Newcastle legs from 18 yards when a long throw was headed out to the edge of the box.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

Collison between Van Ewijk and Willock leaves them both winded and needing treatment. The Newcastle midfielder had been trying to bullock down the middle in purusit of a pass.

Coventry overload with seven men on the right before rolling the kick-off to the left-footed Rushworth who launches it too far up that wing and Hornicek gathers.

Interesting half for Matias Fernandez-Pardo who has been in the middle of most of Newcastle’s best moments but has failed to take two excellent chances.

It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1366. Michael Carrick accepts he won't be given time to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson as Unai Emery confirms Aston Villa contract talks in blow to Man United: Premier League LIVE

Published: 06:57 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 10:06 EDT, 6 November 2026

It's the final Premier League gameweek before the international break, and managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press.

Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here...

Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman is raring to impress with the England Under 21s after being called up for the first time.

The 16-year-old Arsenal attacker has been selected by head coach Lee Carsley for the November friendlies against Portugal and France, with Dowman having previously represented England up to Under 19 level.

Should he feature in one of the matches, the teenager would become the youngest player to represent England's Under 21s, surpassing the record set by Jude Bellingham.

Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman is raring to impress with the England Under 21s next week

Arteta said: 'It's great news, I think he's very excited about that and now he has another contribution to do with the national team.

'Unfortunately, he cannot play for us in the next few games, but he will have the chance to play with the national team, which is great.'

Michael Carrick believes it's possible to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Manchester United, but accepts he won't be given as much time to turn the club's fortunes around as his former boss.

On the 40th anniversary of Ferguson replacing Ron Atkinson in 1986 with United one place above the relegation zone, Carrick's team are in an identical position having equalled Atkinson's club record worst start of one win from the first nine games.

A rousing win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday has lifted the mood around Old Trafford and eased some of the pressure on Carrick ahead of Sunday's game at home to Aston Villa.

Ferguson survived a barren three-and-a-half years in charge before winning the FA Cup in 1990. It was the first over 38 trophies over more than quarter of a century, and Carrick was asked if it would be impossible to match that.

'Well, it's not impossible,' said Carrick. 'Anything's possible. You've got to build, you know. You've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well. The recent history that we've had and where we want to get to, it's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight. Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time. But it does take a period of time to build.'

Asked if he will be given the same amount of time as Ferguson after 10 months in charge, Carrick replied: 'The game's certainly changed, no doubt. It always does. It had evolved to the stage probably after Sir Matt (Busby) in the years after that, to then Sir Alex.

'It evolves all the time. That's how it is. It changes. We've got to deal with what's in front of us. I get the comparisons. I understand it. There are always different things to compare, but it's we've always got to live in the present as well.

Michael Carrick accepts he won't be given time to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United

'Definitely use past experiences to help us, but we're all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as you possibly can.'

It was suggested that the 3-2 comeback win over Roma could be Carrick's 'Mark Robins moment' in reference to the striker's FA Cup winner against Nottingham Forest that was said to have saved Ferguson from the sack.

'More comparisons, yeah,' smiled Carrick. 'You always find something to compare, don't you? It's up to us to take it forward, you know. It was a fantastic night.

'It was nice for the supporters to end like that and to have that feeling, one hundred per cent for sure.

'But nothing's achieved yet, and it's one moment really in time that we need to use to move forward. But we need more of it, for sure.'

On Ferguson's 40th anniversary at United and his relationship with the Scot these days, Carrick said: 'What has not been said already? It's something definitely worth celebrating as a football club. That it's 40 years this week since he came here, and the impact on the football club, moving forward for all the time that he was here and that he's left for others to carry forward is incredible.

'I'm probably closer to him now and speak more to him now than I did when I was playing. I think the relationships change over time and that's only natural. Ever since I came here, the impact he had on me as an individual was immense.

'Not necessarily directly as in talking all the time and advice all the time. Personally, it was more the influence that he had and the habits that you try and pick up from him, as did everyone around the football club over that period of time. Then you move on and evolve a little bit into a friendship, which is really nice.'

Carrick confirmed that new £70million signing Carlos Baleba will be out for a 'number of weeks' after injuring his right hamstring against Roma, and United will wait to see if Patrick Dorgu can be involved against Villa after returning to training following a hamstring strain of his own.

Unai Emery has confirmed he intends to sign a new long-term deal with Aston Villa – ending Manchester United's hopes of hiring him if they sack Michael Carrick.

The Villa boss' current contract expires in 2029 and ahead of Sunday's meeting with United, Emery intends to extend the arrangement after positive talks with co-owner Nassef Sawiris.

'We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a [new] deal, yes,' he said. 'Nassef is very ambitious, a hard worker and his commitment to the club is huge. It's easy for me to have meetings with him as normally we are on the same page.

'It's about increasing our budget each year, and our revenue. Improving players, selling players, buying young talented players. This is the process and vision we should keep for the future.

'I had a very good, positive meeting with Nassef. Let's talk next week, trying to get everything that we have spoken about together.'

United's admiration for Emery has created a storm. Villa threatened to sue Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher for telling fans to 'shut the f*** up'. Supporters had objected to Carragher arguing that Emery should join United to further his career, and Carragher apologised for his crude language.

Villa's announcement on Wednesday that Sawiris and Emery had held talks also felt like a warning shot towards United.

Unai Emery has confirmed he intends to sign a new long-term deal with Aston Villa

Emery has never won at Old Trafford as Villa boss and despite United's poor form he remains wary.

He said: 'It's Manchester United. We haven't won one match there in the four years I've been here.

'It's very difficult for us. It's a fantastic club. They performed very well last year to get into the Champions League.

'This year in the league they've not been consistent at the start but they should recover. We played Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday and this game is of the same level.'

Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form with Manchester City's No 1 amid a number of high-profile errors.

Donnarumma was flat-footed in being beaten at his near post during Wednesday's Champions League win at RB Leipzig, following mistakes against Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa.

City's manager does not see the value in raking over the issues with his goalkeeper and believes the Italian's confidence is still high.

'He's good, overall he's good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma's mood. 'He's quite relaxed, in terms of recognising that he has done some mistakes but has made some good saves.

'There are players that when they make mistakes you need conversation with them, and there are players that when they make some mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises.

'With Gigio it's quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately. Sometimes you don't need to be so deep with some players.'

Meanwhile, Maresca insisted that Elliot Anderson has another level to reach after an encouraging start to his City career.

Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form

The £116million summer signing goes back to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, with Maresca claiming that Oliver Glasner's side are in a false position.

'Elliot can do many [more] things, but he knows that,' Maresca added. 'We had a conversation before the last Champions League game, a nice conversation on understanding the game and slowly he is getting better and better.

'Elliot in this moment is playing more as the holding midfielder, but in future he can also play a little bit more up front.'

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has backed Josh King to make the most of his 'special moment' after being called up to the England squad for the first time.

The 19-year-old has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for the upcoming Nations League games, having continued to impress this season after being part of England's pre-World Cup camp.

'It is a special moment for him and also for us as a club and our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and supporters,' Arbeloa said at a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League game against Newcastle.

'He came to this club when he was eight and now you look at how he is playing and performing, so we are really proud of him. It is a big step for him and I am so happy for him because he is a very humble kid. You can see every day he wants to improve, to work and become a better player.'

King will again be central to Fulham's gameplan when Arbeloa's side take on Newcastle looking to build some momentum following last weekend's battling 1-1 draw at Aston Villa.

'For me, he is a very talented player. He can receive between the lines where there is no space,' Arbeloa said. 'He can drive, he can run, he can dribble with the ball, so he has everything, and we are working with him about his finishing.

'Obviously he needs to improve there and it is the most difficult thing in football, scoring goals, but his mentality, his character, he is a very mature player. You can't forget that he is just 19 years old, so it is unbelievable how he is performing. I think he has everything to become one of the best players in the world.'

After losing their last home game 1-0 to strugglers Crystal Palace, Arbeloa is expecting a response back at Craven Cottage. 'We know how difficult it will be to beat Newcastle tomorrow, they are a very good team, but we are playing well,' said the Fulham boss, who will be without defender Timothy Castagne because of a knee issue.

#1364. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

To qualify for the World Cup finals in Brazil, England must navigate a two-stage play-off system. Beating Greece over two legs is only step one; the winner will advance to face either Slovakia or Ukraine in a December decider.

Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1363. Jude Bellingham's brother Jobe gets first England call-up - as Thomas Tuchel explains axeing Cole Palmer, who 'misses too many opportunities to impress': Squad announcement RECAP

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

I think eight hours of coverage for the England squad announcement is enough, don't you?

In all seriousness, it's been real. Enjoy your weekend and thank you for joining us today.

One player I haven't mentioned yet is Dan Burn.

He became one of Thomas Tuchel's favourite picks in the backline last year prior to the World Cup. Then, of course, he played a huge part in that famous win over Mexico in the round of 16.

But it seems the Newcastle man can't get a look in anymore, after being omitted from Tuchel's squad today following being left out in the last extended break.

Tuchel has said it was a 'difficult phone call' with Burn because they have obviously formed a bond, but for now the big man just isn't in his plans.

Will we ever see Burn play for England again?

On whether Palmer regrets missing last international break:

Enzo Maresca, Manchester City boss, on Phil Foden being left out:

It's now been a couple of hours since we heard from Thomas Tuchel, so I think it's worth a quick recap of the biggest lines from his presser.

Let's take a look at who the big inclusions and omissions are in this squad because there are a few.

Thomas Tuchel on Ben White being booed back in March:

It's going to be interesting to see the reaction to Ben White's first touch as an England player again.

Back in March, when he first returned from his exile, there were huge boos from the Wembley crowd. They were clearly on Gareth Southgate's side and not White's.

But they can't boo their own forever. White may have missed the World Cup through injury, but I expect him to become England's No.1 right-back under Thomas Tuchel; the German clearly likes him.

Tuchel has made it clear he wants White well supported, not booed.

#1362. Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 49–57 (2026) Cite this article

The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III–V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

#1361. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

This touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo

“We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta said. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta said. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

In the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi

It took a while. Arteta got ever more sour in his dealings with Richard Hempel, the giant German fourth official. Bruno Guimarães hustled as best he could in midfield and might have won a penalty. But essentially Arsenal lacked the subtle attacking edge that distinguishes the best from the rest in this competition. You could see it immediately in the way that Odegaard hunted for the ball for the second goal and then turned urgently to attack Lille. The third goal was a passing sequence from Saka to Odegaard to Havertz and back to Saka for the finish.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo

The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Lille thought they'd taken the lead at the Emirates, but it's ruled out for offside ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/c0k49kH5sn

The goals came quickly after the hour. First Timber’s delicately lifted chip over Ozer from Madueke’s ball. Eze ran onto a left-foot shot from Saka’s pass to score four minutes later. Soon after that Arsenal sliced Lille open a third time and Saka took a touch in the area before finishing.

Arteta starts his press conference with a tribute to Ken Friar: "There are people in football clubs that create an identity, create values and have a vision to create a future. The legacy that Ken is going to leave, to all of us and to our club, is going to be forever."

A few things tactically: one adjustment attacking, one defending. But especially, that we had to increase the technical level. At this level, the teams are really well organised. We gave simple ball;s away, bad touches mistimed things. When we delivered the ball into the box it wasn’t the right area so we get caught, especially delivering from the right and [Lille] transition on the left.

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. This was not their most fluent or creative performance, but sheer weight of pressure told and Lille cracked. The away team could not get out of their defensive third after half time, and after Timber’s goal the class of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard from the bench took over.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

Just the three minutes of added time to play. Havertz has just been booked for catching the goalkeeper Ozer who was dallying on the ball.

Odegaard with a delightful first-time pass around the corner to Dowman, but the youngster cut inside looking for his goal and his shot was blocked. Maybe he could have looked for Saka across goal.

Arsenal happy to usher this game to a conclusion now. Dowman had one chance to run at the Lille defence from the right, but he played a pass expected a Havertz run that never came.

Max Dowman is now on for Eze. Saka will finish the game on the left, with Dowman on the right.

An extra treat for the Arsenal fans who have not made an early exit: Mikel Arteta is about to bring on Max Dowman. This feels like a presentable opportunity for a first Champions League goal, Lille have been non-existent in this half.

The yellow card is coming out for Lille’s Goffi, who catches the inside of Eze’s ankle with his studs. The tackle did not quite have enough force to be worthy of a red card.

Bruno Guimaraes stings the palms of Ozer with a strike from the edge of the box, when perhaps he could have looked for Saka.

Olivier Giroud is on now for Lille, and he receives a standing ovation from most of the Emirates. A rarity when a former player returns.

Arteta has made another change: Ben White replaces Timber.

Big block by Ezri Konsa to help preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet, but Lille are still to have a shot on target. They were competitive in the first half, but have found the intensity too much too handle in the second 45 minutes.

That will answer some questions about his finishing, Arsenal’s No 7 rolls the ball into the bottom corner and they have scored three in seven second-half minutes. Slick combination play involving Timber, Odegaard and Havertz down the right, and the German played a cute ball back to Saka and he finished in style.

Arsenal have scored quite a few lovely team goals so far this season, including against Leeds United a few days ago. That was another one. The combination of Saka, Odegaard and Havertz was too much for Lille to handle. The arrival of those three substitutes has massively enhanced Arsenal’s attack.

A finish worthy of any striker. Would it be harsh to say it’s the kind of finish Arsenal’s actual striker has never looked like providing?

Arsenal have been working the ball into those positions inside the penalty box all game long, and finally it brings the breakthrough. There aren’t many defenders who can control and finish as cleanly as that, in a penalty box as crowded as it was there. A classy goal.

Odegaard and Saka are getting themselves ready on the bench, the changes are incoming.

Excellent recovery from Rice to snuff a Lille break, the ball just keeps coming back at the French side.

If anything, Arsenal have been almost too dominant. The game is a 10vs10 on the edge of the Lille box with no space.

Bruno Guimaraes has been Arsenal’s most enterprising player, and he has just gone down looking for a penalty. I think he was looking for it, and the on-field decision of no penalty stands. The defender may have trailed a leg, but it was unconvincing attempt from Guimaraes. Sam disagrees though!

I’m surprised that wasn’t given as a penalty. Looked like a clear movement into Bruno’s path, with no contact on the ball.

Arsenal completely dominant now, without producing a final pass or shot of any great quality. Lille’s goalkeeper Ozer has not had to make a save in this spell despite all this possession. Lille penalised for taking too long over a throw, before Madueke’s shot is deflected through to Ozer.

Very obvious foul conceded by Gyokeres at the edge of the Lille box just as Arsenal were probing again. Then Bruno Guimaraes wins a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre. They are making hard work of it, but Arsenal do have Lille penned in.

Arsenal play a short one, and Timber is then flagged offside as Eze tries to find him with a reverse pass.

Bruno Guimarães loves a fist-pump to the home supporters and he’s produced a couple here tonight, in an attempt to lift the atmosphere. That’s not to say it’s a bad atmosphere but there is frustration building.

It took a long time for the referee to blow his whistle, but he gives a foul against Madueke on Perraud and Lille can clear their lines after a couple of minutes of Arsenal pressure.

All Arsenal so far in the second half, and they work the ball well into Guimaraes at the edge of the area but he slices his shot wide with his weaker left foot. Feels like the home team are getting closer, though.

Arsenal with another Madueke corner, as they try to apply the pressure. Good delivery into the six-yard box, and it flicks off a Lille head for another corner on the far side. Rice to take.

Headed away. Clever Eze reverse pass to Timber, but crossing with his left foot is not his strong suit and he slices behind.

Arsenal win a corner inside 30 seconds of the second half after a Timber burst forward.

Slow starts have been a theme of late for Arsenal.

Arsenal haven't scored a first-half goal in any of their last five games in the Premier League or Champions League. Their last goal before the break was against Chelsea on 6 September. https://t.co/ZfScceDs6u

The XI on the pitch are trusted to find the opening goal, and that also suggests Arteta is keen to manage minutes.

Barcelona are drawing at Galatasaray and Bayern Munich are 2-0 down against Viking. With Man City playing PSG tomorrow night, these are an important three points for Arsenal to win, relative to the other teams we expect to fill the top spots of the league phase.

It has not been much of a spectacle so far, with Arsenal’s rotated attack stuttering but probably mustering enough chances to have scored by now. Lille managed one moment of danger with the offside goal, but are yet to have a shot on target. A half-time change by Arteta cannot be ruled out.

Great double save from Ozer in the Lille goal after Guimaraes’s shot from distance took a deflection, and he did well to get up and push the ball away from Gyokeres to deny the striker a tap-in.

Andre heads Madueke’s corner behind for another one as half-time approaches. Good delivery to the near post this time but the Lille defence stands firm.

Eze with a loose square ball in midfield, but Arsenal are spared by an offside flag going up against Lille. Arsenal fans wanted the officials to play advantage with a break on.

Corner now for Arsenal. Lovely backheel from Madueke to Timber but his low cross towards Gyokeres is turned behind.

Arsenal yet to score from a corner this season.

Things look like happening for Arsenal when Guimaraes or Eze get on the ball around the top of the penalty area, accessing those areas has been the problem against a well-structured Lille team so far. Arsenal do not look unduly troubled but the home crowd would have expected more so far.

Mikel Arteta is becoming increasingly frustrated on the touchline, primarily with the officiating but one suspects he is also irritated by the wastefulness of his team. The Arsenal manager has, er, expressed some of these emotions to the fourth official, Richard Hempel. But Hempel, who appears to be an absolute German giant of a man, was having none of it. He really towers over Arteta and he wasn’t afraid to play that card.

Big chance for Eze! But he shoots straight at the goalkeeper. The opportunity was created by a lovely defence-splitting pass from Guimaraes through the Lewis-Skelly, who dragged the ball back for Eze. The flag went up for offside, but Lewis-Skelly would have been onside.

Merino with a volley on the turn in the Lille box, but he slices over the bar. Snappy football from Arsenal and Rice to tee up Madueke for the initial cross.

Then Arsenal work the ball patiently from right to left and Eze feeds Lewis-Skelly on the overlap, but his cross is too high and into the goalkeeper’s gloves. That needed to go along the six-yard line.

Eze caught offside after Lewis-Skelly did well to fizz a pass down the line into his feet. Arsenal’s first-choice attackers Odegaard, Saka and Havertz will not be fearing for their places at Forest on the basis of this first half.

Arsenal could do with a little more precision from their front three. Madueke, Eze and Gyokeres have had a few opportunities to hurt Lille but they haven’t done so yet. This is a big night for Eze and Gyokeres, especially, as they largely been marooned on the bench this season.  With Tzolis out, Eze could lock down that left wing slot. But he needs to do more.

Another wasted Arsenal counter-attack, this time Merino turned the wrong way and misplaced a pass before making a frustrated challenge at the expense of a yellow card.

Arsenal probing, without really pulling Lille apart or unduly stressing their defence. Chance on a transition from a midfield giveaway, but Bentaleb did well to show Gyokeres wide and win the ball without conceding a free-kick.

Lille have the ball in Arsenal’s net but the flag goes up for offside! There was a double deflection from a Bentaleb shot, and the ball bounced off Haraldsson straight to Ueda, who finished past Raya from close range. The striker was onside when Bentaleb took his shot, but the second deflection did for him. There was a stoppage for a VAR check, but the decision stands.
