Andrey Santos, one of United’s summer signings, was asked for his thoughts on Lisandro Martínez’s explosive interview in which he took aim at the club’s hierarchy for their strategy in the latest transfer window. The Brazilian said: “We know the comments [of] Licha, but I think now it’s done so we have to move on and focus on tomorrow [Wednesday].

When pressed on whether Martínez had addressed the squad about his remarks, Santos added: “No, no, no. Nothing happened, as you know we are on the same page, so we believe in ourselves, in your team-mates, your coach, your staff, so I think this is the most important.”

Jack Fletcher and Tynan Thompson played for United against Como in the Uefa Youth League earlier in the day and the pair are named among the substitutes. Fletcher played for 71 minutes, and scored, and Thompson the whole game, which United lost 2-1.

It’s happened before where players have played in the Youth League then made the senior bench later in the day although the very youthful bench is a reflection of just how many absentees Carrick has at the moment.

Cesc Fabregas has done a fine job at Como and will hope to further enhance that burgeoning reputation with an historic win. United desperately need results - it’s two wins in 10 in all competitions - and face Bournemouth on Sunday after this.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Absolutely tipping it down in Como, with 64mm of rain forecast before #MUFC kick-off here tomorrow ☔️ https://t.co/WvI3X8dilh

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

#1291. Today’s Papers – Inter, Como and a Scudetto fight

Inter-Como super in una maxi domenica (Inter-Como headlines a huge Sunday)

The Pink Paper leads on tonight’s clash between Inter and Como at San Siro, with Marcus Thuram and Nico Paz on the front page. Gazzetta describes the game as the strength of champions against a wave of attractive football, and says there’s a sense of a Scudetto race between Cristian Chivu’s side and Cesc Fàbregas’ Lariani.

At the top of the page, Roma a tutto gol, Gasp secondo (Roma go all out for goals, Gasp second) celebrates Saturday’s emphatic win over Sassuolo, which moves Gian Piero Gasperini’s side up to second. Teenager Rodrigo Mora is pictured, and the paper notes that the capital now leads the way in Serie A.

Milan are in Genoa this afternoon, and Ritorna il big Milan (The big Milan return) reports that Ruben Amorim will select his first-choice players, from Luka Modrić to Gila, so the Rossoneri don’t slip up again.

The lunchtime game between Napoli and Lazio is billed as Un duello sottosopra (An upside-down duel), with Gennaro Gattuso top of the table and Aurelio De Laurentiis putting the silencer on Massimiliano Allegri.

Juventus are at Fiorentina this evening, and La Signora vuole il 3 (The Old Lady wants three) says Kerim Alajbegović’s Juve are chasing a third consecutive victory.

Elsewhere, Saturday’s round-up is summed up as Vola il Bologna, cade il Frosinone, Toro frenato dal palo (Bologna fly, Frosinone fall, Toro denied by the woodwork).

In Formula 1, Kimi da 10 (A perfect 10 for Kimi) reports that newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli starts on the front row in Brazil as he goes for his 10th win, behind Lando Norris on pole, while the Ferraris have been demoted.

#1290. 'People keep telling me it's great I'm managing against my son... it's not - it's horrible': Peterborough boss ROBBIE SAVAGE and Reading star CHARLIE on their 'awkward' FA Cup showdown, playing for Man United and dangers facing modern young players

Published: 02:00 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EDT, 7 November 2026

The FA Cup cast its spell upon the Savages while they were out shopping for groceries.

Reading midfielder Charlie was strolling the aisles of the Marks & Spencer foodhall with his girlfriend when his phone began to buzz. He remembered it was first-round draw day.

He fished out the phone, saw the cascade of messages and realised, as they like to say in M&S, this was not just any FA Cup draw. He called his dad.

Peterborough United boss Robbie was in the Co-op. He had stopped on his way back to the rented lodgings he describes as a 'little annexe in someone's garden' and was rummaging through the ready meals in search of a spaghetti bolognese for one when he answered.

'The reception in Peterborough isn't great, it kept cutting out,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Charlie said: "You won't believe the draw." I thought he was going to say Forest Green. Or Macclesfield. I didn't think about Reading. He said: "You've got us." I just went: "Oh no."'

They were on a collision course from the moment Robbie left Forest Green for the Posh job last month. The teams were scheduled to meet in League One next month at Reading but the FA Cup draw caught them off guard.

Peterborough boss Robbie Savage (right) with his son, Reading midfielder Charlie. The pair will meet in the FA Cup first round at London Road on Saturday

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport

And while they were both at great pains to stress that Saturday's tie at London Road, screened live on TNT Sports, is about Peterborough and Reading not their little family gathering, they can appreciate the fuss.

'Football is a beautiful game, it brings people together and creates rivalries,' says Charlie. 'This week it's created a rivalry in our family. I'm not sure who my mum, brother, grandparents and cousins will support but there's no better time for them to have a half-and-half scarf.'

For Robbie, the beauty of the occasion is yet to unfurl itself. 'It's going to be horrible,' he says. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling. People keep telling me it's great. I've got to say it's not great, it's horrible. Usually we speak every day and I've not been able to speak to him all week because I don't want to put him in a position where anything gets out and anyone can point a finger at him.

'I don't want it to be billed as Savage v Savage because it's not. Charlie might not play but if he plays and makes a mistake and we score the winner, so be it. If he plays and scores the winner, well, wow.'

Robbie puffs out his cheeks and widens his eyes as he considers this scenario. 'We've got to win for Peterborough United,' he adds.

Ironically, it was a passion relit by coaching his sons which tempted the former Leicester, Birmingham and Blackburn midfielder out of the comfort of his media work and into coaching. Savage helped out with his youngest son Freddie's Under 13s team in the Timperley and District Junior Sunday League.

'Standing out at training on a Tuesday and Thursday night,' says Robbie. 'Sunday morning, putting the nets up. I've been that dad. In the first season we were hammered 13-0, but we built a team and won a lot of things.'

Charlie Savage in action for Reading. The midfielder played 45 games for the club last season but has yet to start a league match during this campaign

Savage offers some advice to his team in his new role as manager of Peterborough

Two years ago, Charlie and Freddie implored their father to follow his heart and make the switch from sporting director to manager at Macclesfield in the Northern Premier League.

'Even back then, he said one day he'd manage against me,' Charlie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I was in League One and he was in Step Three and I'm thinking, "Well, give it a few years", but he always gets where he wants to get to.

'He's a competitor. He wants to win, wants to succeed. Even with my little brother's team it hurt him to lose in Sunday morning grassroots football. That's something inside him and it won't change.

'He will want to beat us. Unfortunately for him, I'm the same. I want to win. There might be an awkward car journey home.'

Charlie's memories of his father playing football are from Derby, the last stop of a 15-year professional career which started at Manchester United and took in seven different clubs, as well as 39 Wales caps. 'I remember seeing his long hair, scurrying around the pitch,' says the 23-year-old. 'Throwing his arms up and shouting at the refs.'

Like his dad, Charlie also came through United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

'He'll always have that on me,' says Robbie. 'All I ever wanted to do from 14 to 19 was play for one minute in Manchester United's first team. It didn't happen and he's done it. His name is on the wall at Carrington and mine isn't.

'I'm so glad his name is there instead of mine. You want the best for your sons. I'm proud of both my sons.'

Charlie has three Wales caps and counting. His father won 39...

...but despite both Charlie and Robbie coming through the Manchester United academy, only Charlie played for the first team (above), against Young Boys at Old Trafford in 2021

Freddie is studying for an economics degree at the University of Manchester. Charlie left United for Reading four years ago and now has 175 senior appearances and three Wales caps under his belt and a reputation in his own right.

'He's got a great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie. 'He's intelligent. Nine As in his GCSEs. He doesn't drink, he lives his life 24 hours a day, seven days a week to be a footballer. He's a down-to-earth, humble kid.

'He was so brave to go and play senior football when he had three years left at Manchester United, and it's paid off. He played 45 games last season. He hasn't started a league game this season but hasn't sulked.

'I was a sulker, as Martin O'Neill and Nigel Clough (who coached Savage at Leicester and Derby respectively) will tell you. If that was me, my body language would be negative, but he's got a great attitude. And I've tried to tell him now he has to train harder than ever and conduct himself in the right way.'

If Robbie is a guiding light and inspiration for Charlie, vital information flows both ways for an aspiring manager with a young team.

'The mindset of a Millennial is completely different to when I played,' says the 52-year-old Posh boss. 'If they're not in the team or the manager has shouted at them, they go home to an apartment where they live alone away from their families, isolated from 2pm to 7am with all that time to think about it.

'We have to understand their vulnerabilities on and off the pitch. Charlie has been through that so without knowing it, he's made me a better manager. I try to think about what's best for my players, what I'd want a manager to do for Charlie in that situation.'

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end,' Charlie says of his dad Robbie

'Great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie of his son Charlie

Being the Son of Sav cannot be easy. Not only the added scrutiny and expectation, and accusations doors have been opened for him by a famous and influential father, but also in a world where footballers are too often considered fair game for abuse whether inside the stadium or online.

'It's there in all forms of life,' admits Charlie. 'Maybe people subconsciously want me to fail a little bit more because of who he is. I get it. Football is a game and my dad is a divisive figure inside that game.

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end. Sometimes the abuse goes too far. People forget he's a human not just a football personality.

'But I wouldn't change who he is. I wouldn't change having him as my dad, I'm very proud of him.'

#1289. Carrick's Key Changes Needed for Man Utd vs Aston Villa

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick might be considering some changes to his side as he looks to turn things around after a disappointing start to the season.

The Red Devils did secure an important 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League during the week, but that's only papered over some of the cracks.

United were still disappointing for large portions of that game and were even 2-0 down after just 18 minutes.

Their Premier League form has been the major disappointment, though, and there's no doubt they drastically need to improve if Carrick wants to save his job, with United's preferred candidate to replace him already named.

Heading towards the game against Chelsea, United have dropped into the relegation zone, having secured just one win all season.

Despite the win over Roma during the week, Carrick is still under pressure at Old Trafford, so it'll be interesting to see whether he makes any major changes to his side.

Many have been calling for Carrick to give a start to young winger Shea Lacey after he came off the bench against Roma to produce an assist.

Starting a young talent like that against Aston Villa does feel unlikely, even though his fearlessness could be what United need.

Lacey might not be the player to make all the difference for United, though.

One player that Carrick needs to bring into the starting eleven is right-back Noussair Mazraoui, who has been barely seen this season, particularly in the Premier League.

Mazraoui's last appearance for United came in the Champions League against Como, but in the Premier League, he's played just 143 minutes.

Mazraoui might not be the difference maker for United, but it could help solve their defensive issues.

The Moroccan international is perhaps being underrated by Carrick, while it would allow Leny Yoro to come back into the centre of defence.

Yoro has been playing in his unfavored position of right-back recently, and although he's performing well there, United need to strengthen the central defence.

Of course, Carrick sees all of these players every single day, but everyone else sees what they produce on the pitch.

It's simply not been good enough for United, and Carrick needs to do something to try to save his job.

He will surely be leaving Manchester United in 2027

The change in defence will allow Carrick to drop centre-back Ayden Heaven from the starting eleven. The young defender conceded a penalty against Roma, and he's generally struggled for the Red Devils.

Heaven is clearly not ready to be playing week in, week out for United, and bringing Mazraoui in will allow the centre of United's defence to look stronger.

There's no doubt Heaven can be a key figure for United in terms of his long-term future, but for now, he shouldn't be a starter.

United will be without Lisandro Martinez for the game against Chelsea due to suspension, but the Mazraoui change could still allow Carrick to drop Heaven.

#1288. Napoli vs. Lazio: Where to watch

Serie A leaders Lazio visit Napoli for Sunday lunchtime, and Max Allegri’s side are under pressure to stop their slide against Gennaro Gattuso’s high-flying Biancocelesti.

It kicks off at 12:30 CET [11:30 GMT] on Sunday at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, with Luca Pairetto as referee.

Lazio are top of Serie A on 28 points. Roma’s 3-0 rout of Sassuolo on Saturday cut their lead to a single point, so Gattuso knows anything less than a win could cost him first place. Their opposition today are 14 points behind on 14, and Allegri is under growing pressure after a 2-0 defeat to Juventus and a 4-1 Champions League loss at Porto.

Napoli also have a long injury list. Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Leonardo Spinazzola, Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno are all out, Mathias Olivera isn’t fully fit, and Luca Marianucci is suspended after his red card in Turin.

Lazio are without captain Mattia Zaccagni and Albert Gudmundsson, while Nuno Tavares is carrying a muscular problem.

In the UK and Ireland, Napoli vs. Lazio is live on DAZN.

#1287. Dele Alli risks the wrath of Spurs fans as he wears an ARSENAL shirt on livestream - with ex-Tottenham star livid after losing bet to influencer iShowSpeed

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 09:49 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:53 EDT, 7 November 2026

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Tottenham supporters after wearing an Arsenal jersey on a Twitch livestream.

The former England midfielder, whose once-bright career has been in freefall since his exit from Tottenham in 2022, has been keeping himself busy on a series of livestreams with fans as he continues to look for a new club.

The 30-year-old star, who has been a free agent since leaving Como in September 2025, joined iShowSpeed on stream after the American influencer challenged him to a game of EAFC 27.

Dele, who played as Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Qadsiah, was beaten 4-2 by iShowSpeed's Al-Nassr and reacted so angrily to missing a late chance that he furiously smashed his controller.

Egged on by the influencer saying, "I ain't gonna lie, throw the controller, break it", as he missed an open goal, the footballer left his chair and started repeatedly launching it against the floor.

Dele's punishment for losing the bet was to wear an Arsenal shirt live on stream, and the former Tottenham midfielder reluctantly obliged.

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Spurs fans after wearing an Arsenal jersey (@dele/instagram)

The ex-Spurs star once said he would rather retire than play for north London rivals Arsenal

Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/62cO7iYm2w

Sporting the jersey of his old team's bitter north London rivals, which had been delivered to his home by a friend, Dele burrowed his head in his hands with discomfort as fans caught a glimpse of him representing Arsenal for the first time.

Gunners supporters were greatly amused as videos and images of Dele, who in 2016 said he would rather retire than play for Arsenal, went viral on social media.

'Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious,' one fan posted to X with a string of laughing emojis.

He later posted a selfie to his Instagram, saying: 'Sorry Spurs fans but a bet is a bet. Congrats iShowSpeed.'

Although a regular streamer nowadays, Dele was once lauded as one of English football's greatest talents, having burst on to the scene under Mauricio Pochettino and carving out almost 200 appearances for the north London club.

He is now making a habit of phoning old team-mates for a chat in front of his audience of followers on stream, having held brief conversations with both Jack Grealish and Tottenham legend Harry Kane.

#1286. 32 Highest-Paid English Footballers in 2026 [Ranked]

Money makes the world go round. And that notion is particularly true for footballers, especially for those earning their corn in the Premier League, as they often take home jaw-dropping amounts of money each week. It has now become a construct that fans and pundits alike tend to converse about. Most notably, whether footballers deserve to be paid much more than their teammates is based on a string of factors.

The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Ivan Toney have seen their weekly salaries rise dramatically since their moves to Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, and the Saudi Pro League respectively. But which Englishmen are receiving eyebrow-raising amounts of money each week? And who, rightly or wrongly, is being paid the most money of all English footballers on the planet?

A goalscoring sensation for Bournemouth, it was no surprise to see Tottenham Hotspur cough up a £60 million fee for the sharpshooting Dominic Solanke in the summer of 2024. Since, the Basingstoke-born striker – capped three times at international level – has scored 24 times for Spurs. Like many on this list, the centre-forward has had to contend with a number of injury issues.

Such problems have limited his influence for Ange Postecoglou, Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor and now Roberto De Zerbi. Irrespective of how many matches he's played, he still earns £140,000-per-week. On the international stage, Solanke faces the challenge of competing with Kane for a starting berth – and, as a result, his caps have been restricted to just three.

Tammy Abraham made his return to English football in January 2026 after five years away. The Chelsea academy product, who scored 25 league goals for Aston Villa in the 2018/19 season as they won promotion back to the Premier League, completed a £18m transfer to the Villans.

He's scored plenty of goals for the club before, but has netted just twice in the league so far in his second spell at Villa Park. Villa need him to step up and be counted following the departure of Ollie Watkins and many other key players.

Having developed through Villa's academy, the 25-year-old exited for Tyneside after failing to get regular game time at Villa Park. A fee of around £43million was enough for the Magpies to add the talented midfielder to their ranks, but he has failed to catch fire so far.

Wholesale squad changes, exits and a new manager, plus injury niggles have combined to leave him struggling to find the kind of momentum that saw him heralded as a potential future England star. There is plenty of work to be done for Ramsey, as he looks to settle, find his feet and justify the £150,000-per-week that he's currently contracted for.

Mason Mount, now of Manchester United, was much further down this list while playing for his boyhood club, Chelsea. The playmaker was signed by the Red Devils in the summer of 2023 and now receives a cool £150,000-per-week in Manchester. Only a handful of players at Old Trafford take home more than the injury-prone Englishman.

His first few years in Manchester have left a lot to be desired, though his progression has been halted by a string of fitness problems. Still just 27 years of age, Mount has recorded eight goals and two assists since making the intra-Premier League switch to the Theatre of Dreams.

Carrick's system is far more beneficial to him than previous managers, but getting into the team is still proving to be a difficult task. Bruno Fernandes essentially has his dream role, which won't be changing anytime soon. Still, across four competitions, if he stays fit there's chances to prove himself once again. Whether he's able to repay his weekly wage remains unknown.

There’s an awful lot of unjust discourse over Jordan Pickford’s position between the sticks for England, isn’t there? For years, Everton’s shot-stopper has been the nation’s first choice – and, well, he’s rarely put a glove wrong. Some supporters, however, are not as convinced about the talents of Pickford, who has racked up 93 appearances for the Three Lions.

For the Toffees, the 32-year-old has been equally integral. Albeit not the tallest of goalkeepers, his combination of shot-stopping and leadership is perfect for the Merseysiders. At the time of writing, the glovesman earns £150,000-per-week and, on a separate note, he’s Everton’s highest-earning asset and an undroppable figure at international level.

The last few years of Kalvin Phillips' career can hardly have gone as he would have expected. The defensive midfielder – who earns £150,000 every week – spent eight years with boyhood club Leeds United, rising to prominence in Marcelo Bielsa's system and style of play. Such was his form that it caught the eye of Pep Guardiola and Manchester City, who moved to sign him in 2022.

Despite his calibre, Phillips struggled to break into the City first team given that Rodri was ahead of him in the pecking order. Minimal minutes led to unsuccessful loan spells at West Ham United, Ipswich Town and Sheffield United. Despite his struggles, the Blades decided to take him on loan once again for the 2026/27 campaign.

There were times when big doubts came up about whether Luke Shaw was the man to start at left-back in the long term for Manchester United. He was regularly criticised by Jose Mourinho, but has since silenced his loudest critics with excellent performances that have made him the starting left-back for his club once more when fit.

Arguably the best English player at Old Trafford, injuries plagued his progress under Erik ten Hag throughout the 2023/24 campaign and the same followed under Ruben Amorim. Are his days at Old Trafford numbered? Perhaps, but he has found better form under Michael Carrick in recent times.

After the Poole-born defender signed a brand-new bumper contract in March 2024, Ben White has proven his innate versatility by playing out of his natural position. A centre-back by trade, the Englishman had previously nailed down a regular starting position for the Gunners – but as a full-back. His influence, of course, has waned in recent times, partly due to injury issues, and he is no longer top of the pecking order.

The 29-year-old, who pockets £150,000-per-week, took to his new role like a duck to water, but he's since been dislodged by Jurrien Timber. He might not offer the same creativity as the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold, but when it comes to a mix of attacking and defending, there aren't many right-backs better in the league than a fit White.

Is Noni Madueke a player waiting to explode? Some would suggest so; some would suggest that his poor form for Chelsea was exactly what the 24-year-old winger can provide a Premier League side. Alas, Mikel Arteta and Arsenal saw him as a forward able to provide something different from a forward-thinking perspective – and the Londoner has performed well for the Gunners.

So far, despite not being a regular starter for the north Londoners, Madueke has been a constant thorn for defences up and down the country, but 11 goals in 55 Arsenal appearances suggest room for improvement. From a wages' perspective, he earns £160,000 per-week with the Gunners as a backup to Bukayo Saka.

#1284. Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney jet in to watch clash with Wolves after surprise exit of club's CEO - and catch up with poppy-protest footballer James McClean in the stands

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:39 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 10:40 EDT, 7 November 2026

Wrexham's celebrity owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have travelled to watch their side's Championship clash with Wolves less than a day after announcing chief executive Michael Williamson's surprise departure.

Reynolds and McElhenney announced in a joint statement on Friday that Williamson was leaving the club after two years at the Racecourse Ground, with club director Shaun Harvey set to take the reins as acting CEO while they seek a successor.

'We thank Michael Williamson for his two years at Wrexham and for his work taking the club from League 1 to the Championship,' the Hollywood actors' statement read.

'Since our takeover five years ago, Wrexham have had historic success on the pitch and won hearts all over the globe.

'We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud.

'Shaun Harvey has been an integral part of this journey from the beginning, and we know Shaun will give every support to (manager) Phil Parkinson and the lads on the pitch while keeping the broader Wrexham community roaring us on.'

Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds pictured watching Wrexham take on Wolves on Saturday

The American actor takes photos with supporters as he arrives at the Racecourse Ground

Williamson arrived at Wrexham in 2024 and oversaw a period that saw the club win promotion from League One to the Championship and consolidate themselves in the second tier, narrowly missing out on the playoffs with a seventh-place finish.

Wrexham's form this campaign has been less fruitful, with just four wins so far leaving Parkinson's side in 17th place heading into Saturday's clash with Wolves.

After arriving and meeting fans outside the stadium, Reynolds and McElhenney took their place in the Racecourse Ground stands hoping to watch their Wrexham side earn back-to-back wins for the first time this season.

Wolves, who were relegated from the Premier League last season, took the lead in the 25th minute before Wrexham's Lewis O'Brien equalised moments later, to the delight of the celebrity owners.

As the matched ebbed and flowed, both sides fought hard for a winning goal but ended up settling for a share of the spoils, the 1-1 draw moving Wrexham to 15th and Wolves to third in the Championship.

After the match, Parkinson backed Harvey to adapt seamlessly to his new temporary CEO role, saying:  'Ryan spoke to me yesterday morning to let me know the news. I had a brief chat with Shaun this morning; he has been an important figure. He understands everything about the club.'

While watching the 1-1 draw, Reynolds was pictured chatting to former Wrexham star James McClean, who left the Racecourse Ground to join his hometown team Derry City in January.

McClean's appearance at Wrexham is particularly poignant on Remembrance Weekend, given the controversy he courted throughout his career by refusing to wear football shirts featuring a poppy.

Reynolds pictured chatting to former Wrexham footballer James McClean in the stands

Wrexham players, displaying poppies, observe a minute of silence on Remembrance weekend

Clubs across English football will observe a period of silence before matches this weekend, with players also wearing poppy-adorned shirts to honour those who lost their lives in conflict.

McClean's objection to wearing a poppy is rooted in his upbringing in Derry, having grown up on the Creggan estate, where six of the 13 civilians shot dead by British soldiers on Bloody Sunday in 1972 were from.

#1283. Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

Villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s new-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg

Despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

Villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up issues against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

We’ll bring you the latest updates and drama. Kick-off is at 20:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1282. Genoa vs. Milan: probable line-ups and where to watch

Luka Modrić, Christian Pulisic and Mario Gila are expected to start for Milan at Genoa as Ruben Amorim shakes things up after Thursday’s defeat, while former Rossoneri Stephan El Shaarawy and Lorenzo Colombo start for Daniele De Rossi’s side.

The match kicks off at 15:00 CET [14:00 GMT] on Sunday at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, with Davide Massa as referee.

Milan won the derby last weekend but came back down to earth on Thursday, losing 2-0 at home to Ferencváros in the Europa League. Amorim is expected to make several changes in response, with Gila, Diego Moreira, Modrić and Pulisic all set to start as the Rossoneri try to keep pace in the race for the top four. They are fifth in Serie A on 21 points.

Milan have a long absentee list. Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Fikayo Tomori and Pietro Terracciano are all out. Samuel Chukwueze has had hip surgery and faces around three months on the sidelines, and Strahinja Pavlović has been ruled out.

Genoa have only Nuredini to assess, while Leo Østigård is one booking away from a suspension.

There are a couple of selection doubts. Gazzetta have Pervis Estupiñán at left-back, but Goal tip Davide Bartesaghi to start there. For Genoa, Tommaso Baldanzi is ahead of Wiafe in midfield, and Colombo is narrowly favoured over Vitinha up front.

In the UK and Ireland, Genoa vs. Milan is live on DAZN.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Østigård, Vásquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traoré, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajić. Coach: De Rossi

Milan (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupiñán; Musah, Modrić; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos. Coach: Amorim

#1281. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.

Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.

Arteta will be very disappointed by how Bayern were able to find Kane free in the middle from a throw-in. Whether Konsa should have been higher or Madueke further across, it was too simple.

A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. The bigger story for Arsenal is the thigh injury suffered by Saka. It would be very surprising to see him before the November international break, at best. He pulled up abruptly.

Arsenal caught out on the break by Harry Kane taking a goal kick, from which he picked out Davies with a raking pass down the left. Saibari helped the ball on for Gnabry who was free on the right, but Raya was down quickly to save and Rice cleared.

Arsenal have a corner, after a nice Madueke backheel released Timber. They have the upper hand in this game, but they have lost a major attacking reference with Saka going off. Arsenal enjoying the lion’s share of possession so far, which is perhaps a reflection of Bayern’s absentees. Kane has just dropped into his own box to receive a pass, and Konsa followed him all the way.

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Bayern Munich starting XI: Neuer, Stanisic, Kim Minjae, Upamecano, Davies, Pavlovic, Laimer, Bischof, Gnabry, Saibari, Kane

There was little doubt that Arteta would view this game as one that suits Jurrien Timber rather than Ben White. Arsenal’s manager has changed tack by starting Calafiori, who was rested for Arsenal’s first two Champions League games, but Bayern at the Allianz is a significant step up in grade. Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Madueke

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Two changes for tonight's test ✊

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1280. Roberto De Zerbi questions Tottenham's character and demands 'honest' Leeds debrief after wilting at Elland Road: 'We won no duels, no one-to-ones, we deserved to lose'

Published: 10:59 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EDT, 7 November 2026

Roberto De Zerbi questioned Tottenham’s character after his side’s second-half surrender saw them slip to defeat at Leeds.

Noah Okafor’s late strike sealed the points for the home side as Spurs – who played encouragingly before the break – had no answer to the home side’s rhythm.

De Zerbi said: ‘In the second half, I don’t know why, we suffered too much and deserved to lose. We won no duels, no one-to-ones. There was space to play and we didn’t take the right decisions.

‘We didn’t show personality or what we are, who we are. It’s a part of the journey. It’s not an excuse and it can be normal in football but we have to be honest.

‘If you are not honest today the future is not good. If we analyse our second-half behaviour honestly then I think we can become a top team.

‘We have the physicality and the quality but it’s not just about the physicality game. We didn’t show character, personality or courage.

Roberto De Zerbi says his Spurs side lacked 'character and courage' in their 1-0 loss to Leeds

Noah Okafor netted the winner for the hosts at Elland Road as Spurs lost control of the game

‘My players have the ability to come here, play better and maybe win. But maybe we are not ready yet to be consistent for many games in a row. We know where we have to work and improve.

‘I was surprised by the second half as my players worked very well this week. We spoke all week about the intensity and the type of game we would find here in this stadium so it was not a surprise for us.’

De Zerbi also feared Mathys Tel has suffered a bad injury following a tackle from Jayden Bogle at the end of the first half that was checked by VAR for a possible red card.

Tel was forced off after Bogle’s studs made heavy contact with his ankle, and will undergo scans. De Zerbi would not be drawn on whether Bogle should have been shown a red card but said referee John Brooks’ ‘parameters were not good enough’ in handling the situation.

#1279. Inter vs. Como: probable line-ups and where to watch

Marcus Thuram and Francesco Pio Esposito are expected to lead the line for Inter against high-flying Como, while Nico Paz and hat-trick hero Tasos Douvikas should start for Cesc Fàbregas’ side at San Siro.

Inter vs. Como kicks off at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT] on Sunday at San Siro, with Daniele Chiffi as referee.

It’s one of the games of the season so far. Third-placed Inter are on 25 points, only two ahead of Como, who would go above Cristian Chivu’s side with a win. Both teams come into the game in form in Europe: Inter bounced back from their derby defeat with a 3-0 win at Feyenoord, while Como made Champions League history with a 9-1 thrashing of Lens, the biggest away win in the competition’s history.

Alessandro Bastoni returns from suspension for Inter, and John Stones and Curtis Jones are fit again but likely to start on the bench. Lautaro Martínez and Luis Henrique are still out.

Como’s injury list is longer. Assane Diao, Jesús Rodríguez, Moise Kean and Addai are unavailable, and Trevoh Chalobah is unlikely to be fit in time.

Chivu still has several decisions to make. Gazzetta have Petar Sučić in midfield, but Goal expect Piotr Zieliński to start after he scored in Rotterdam. Spence vs. Diouf, Dimarco vs. Carlos Augusto and Esposito vs. Ange-Yoan Bonny are all close calls. For Como, Jean Butez is expected to keep his place in goal ahead of Sanchez, and Martin Baturina is a strong favourite over Maxence Caqueret.

In the UK and Ireland, Inter vs. Como is live on DAZN and TNT Sports 4, with streaming on HBO Max.

In Italy, the game is on DAZN and Sky Sport.

Inter (3-5-2): J. Martínez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Çalhanoğlu, Sučić, Dimarco; Pio Esposito, Thuram. Coach: Chivu

Como (4-2-3-1): Butez; Couto, Ramón, Kempf, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Nico Paz, Baturina; Douvikas. Coach: Fàbregas

#1278. A death sentence for ‘sloppy’ cancers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Lorenzo Valcanover is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands.

Reuven Agami is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands, and the Department of Genetics, Erasmus University Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

Identifying cellular properties that distinguish a cancer from healthy tissue is a crucial step for developing efficient treatments. One such characteristic is the ‘sloppy’ way in which some cancer cells implement translation — the process by which proteins are made from messenger RNA by protein complexes called ribosomes. This process can go awry. Writing in Nature, Wang et al.1 reveal a cancer-specific mechanism by which translation loses its normal ‘track’ of how it reads an mRNA sequence to encode the expected amino acids, resulting in a phenomenon called frameshifting. This generates proteins that have a distinct sequence of amino acids that are not usually made, and the authors show that this abnormality might be exploited for therapeutic purposes.

#1277. Tottenham are proof that a truckload of NFL and Beyonce cash is no use if you don't spend it properly, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - after Roberto De Zerbi's £500m team saw their mini-revival ended by Leeds

Published: 09:34 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EDT, 7 November 2026

Clubs outside European football’s elite are convinced the game’s financial rules are rigged to protect the richest and keep out the pretenders.

But Tottenham are living proof that making a truckload of money from Beyonce concerts and NFL fixtures is no use if you do not spend it properly.

A decade ago, Spurs fans complained frequently that Daniel Levy would not loosen the purse strings. At the time, the club was riding high under Mauricio Pochettino but could not take the final jump that – perhaps – a world-class signing or two would have delivered.

On reflection, perhaps the hierarchy were right back then. Maybe if they had worked within tighter limits in recent years, they might have made more sensible decisions in the market.

Tottenham’s starting XI at Leeds cost the best part of £500million with Leeds’ barely a quarter of that. It did not stop substitute Noah Okafor settling a tight game late in the second half and ending Spurs’ mini-revival.

Consider Pochettino’s Tottenham side at its peak. We’re not talking just Harry Kane, but Mousa Dembele, Kyle Walker, Christian Eriksen and Danny Rose. Hugo Lloris, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Dele Alli and Heung-min Son.

Not many of the current crop would make it anywhere that team which is rather worrying when we consider the sums Tottenham have invested.

Leeds United leapfrogged Tottenham into the top half of the Premier League table

Roberto De Zerbi saw his side's three-game winning run come to an end at Elland Road

The problem with this squad is that they have a whole heap of players in the ‘good-to-very good’ bracket, who are largely interchangeable among themselves. A few, like Micky van de Ven, James Maddison, Sandro Tonali and potentially Mateus Fernandes, are a little above that category. There is nobody, though, who you could truly call world class.

Take Roberto De Zerbi, too. A bright, talented boss who did commendable work at Sassuolo, Shakhtar Donetsk, Brighton and Marseille. He does not, however, belong to the top rank like Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Unai Emery or – increasingly – Mikel Arteta.

Here, Okafor scored the only goal barely a minute after coming on, combining with fellow sub Harry Wilson and slotting beyond Antonin Kinsky. Leeds made most of the chances in the second half and ended a five-match run without a win, though James Trafford saved Jan Paul van Hecke’s header late on to preserve the points.

Spurs have enough talent to keep them well clear of relegation and it is the kind of squad who can make a strong cup run. That is what Spurs have often been in modern times and there is nothing essentially wrong with it. Given the cash the current regime have splashed, though, they may just expect a little more.

Every summer, they do it. They tweak, fiddle and fuss. They preach about high bars, mic up officials and apologise to angry managers.

They have even changed the name of their organisation from PGMOL to Pro Ref, but they will never remove the controversy that VAR causes nearly every weekend.

Towards the end of the first half, Mathys Tel screamed in pain after Jayden Bogle fouled him. Replays showed Bogle’s studs make a solid contact with the Frenchman’s ankle but after nearly five minutes of checking, referee John Brooks was told to stick with his original decision.

‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Bogle escaped because there was ‘a lack of speed going into the challenge’ which VAR Tony Harrington deemed ‘reckless’ rather than dangerous. Whatever it was, Tel was injured moments later and Leeds had got away with one. Tel will have scans and De Zerbi fears the worst.

In real time, it looked a standard foul. After re-watching, though, it was hard to see how Bogle could stay on the pitch.

For all the decisions VAR overturns correctly, there are still far too many that leave too many people baffled.

‘I can’t say more as I didn’t see the situation clearly but I was surprised to see Pedro Porro given a yellow card in the second half for a foul in a similar position,’ said De Zerbi. ‘I don’t know if [Bogle’s] foul should be a red card or not but today the parameters of the referee were not good enough for these situations.’

Leeds are planning to expand Elland Road, but the stadium must not lose its raw essence

Leeds are working to increase the size of Elland Road and hope that the capacity will eventually be 53,000. Whatever they do, they must not damage the place’s raw essence.

Only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have a better points-per-game record than Leeds since Daniel Farke became boss in 2023. The lunchtime kick-off will never match the floodlit fixture for atmosphere but the second half here was as raucous as on its best days, and the stadium shook when Okafor slotted the winner past Antonin Kinsky.

‘When you have a few games without the winning feeling, it’s always difficult,’ Farke admitted. ‘Heading into the international break, it’s important to win again.’

There is plenty to improve for Leeds. If Dominic Calvert-Lewin catches a cold, where do the goals come from? Who can replace what Ethan Ampadu provides in the centre of midfield?

These are questions for Farke to tackle but with Elland Road at his team’s back, he has solid foundations on which to build.

Leeds (3-5-2): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 7, MUHAREMOVIC 8; Bogle 7 (Rodon 90+3), Longstaff 6 (Gruev 90+2), Ampadu 7, Tanaka 6 (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 46, 7); Calvert-Lewin 7, Nmecha 6 (Okafor 77).

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 7; Porro 6 (Gallagher 65, 6), Van Hecke 7, Van de Ven 7, Robertson 6; Fernandes 6 (Bentancur 65, 6), Tonali 7; Kudus 6 (Williams-Barnett 83), Gray 6, Tel 6 (Solanke 43, 6); Marmoush 5 (Kulusevski 65, 6).

#1275. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EDT, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

#1273. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1272. Epileptic seizures nearly vanish after people receive experimental gene therapy in their brains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mariana Lenharo is a reporter for Nature in New York City.

A scan shows the brain of a man with epilepsy. A newly developed gene therapy targets locations in the brain that are the root of epileptic seizures. Credit: Allison Robbert/The Washington Post/Getty

Three people with epilepsy resistant to drug treatment saw the number of seizures they had per month fall by more than 90% after gene-laden viruses were infused directly into their brains as part of an early-stage clinical trial1.

In each participant, the gene therapy was precisely targeted to a small patch of brain tissue that was the source of their seizures. The viruses carried a gene that makes neurons sensitive to a specific drug, which works like a dimmer switch for the therapy. By combining gene therapy with a drug — an approach known as chemogenetics — researchers can adjust a treatment’s potency, which is not possible with other types of gene therapy. The trial participants did not experience serious side effects.

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

Genetic therapies offer new hope against incurable brain diseases

The results were reported today in The New England Journal of Medicine by Yang Dai, a neurosurgeon at Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University in Beijing, and his colleagues. “It’s exciting that there’s such a dramatic effect, and that they see very few side effects,” says Matthew Walker, a neurologist at University College London, who was not associated with the study.

But Walker cautions that the study is small. He is also concerned about the long-term use of the drug that participants took after receiving the gene therapy. High doses of the drug, an anti-psychotic called clozapine, have been associated with cardiovascular problems and other negative effects. “In the future, hopefully there are going to be better drugs” for this form of treatment, says Walker, who is the co-founder of the start-up company Focalis Bio in Canterbury, UK, which is also developing gene therapies for epilepsy.

The three trial participants were adults with a common form of epilepsy caused by hippocampal sclerosis, a type of scarring in a region of the brain called the hippocampus. The participants had this scarring on only one side of the hippocampus. All three had been diagnosed with epilepsy 10–25 years earlier and had developed resistance to at least two anti-seizure drugs. They also had at least two seizure episodes per month, on average, over the three months before they enrolled in the trial.

The experimental treatment uses a virus called adeno-associated virus 9 to deliver a gene to neurons in the affected area. The gene was engineered to produce proteins specifically in excitatory cells — the ones that are involved in seizures.

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

Brain editing now ‘closer to reality’: the gene-altering tools tackling deadly disorders

The gene instructs neurons to produce a receptor that binds to clozapine. Clozapine acts like a switch and activates these receptors, reducing the activity of the targeted neurons, the authors say. That reduced activity helps to suppress the abnormal electrical activity that triggers seizures.

Two weeks after receiving the gene therapy during surgery, participants began taking a low dose of clozapine every eight hours. Around two months later, the average number of seizures per month had dropped from 4.5 to 0.5 for two of the participants and from 4 to 0 for the third. Because the study design focused on safety, rather than measuring efficacy, there was no control group.

Walker says that there might be other explanations for the improvement. He adds that it is also not clear whether the effect was because of the combination of gene therapy and clozapine or from one of those components alone.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03566-2

Dai, Y. et al. N. Engl. J. Med. 395, 1867–1869 (2026).
