#1271. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EDT, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

#1270. Serie A Liveblog: Napoli-Lazio, Inter-Como, Genoa-Milan, Fiorentina-Juventus and more

Join us for all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games, as Napoli in crisis host leaders Lazio, Milan visit Genoa, there’s Monza-Atalanta, a massive Inter vs. Como clash, then Juventus away to Fiorentina.

Nightmare for Alfonso Pedraza, who turns the ball into his own net just minutes after coming on. Both Hojlund and McTominay went for the ball but it was the Spaniard who got the last touch to knock the ball past Mandas.

Tavares did make way at half-time, with Alfonso Pedraza on in his place.

Second half is underway in Naples as Lazio resume play.

The visitors lead heading into the break, thanks to Frattesi’s quality finish. A few injury troubles for Lazio, though, who lost Sutalo to an apparent hamstring in the first half, with Nuno Tavares also now struggling too.

One additional minute to be played at the end of the first half.

First yellow card of the game goes to Noa Lang after cutting down a promising counter-attack.

DAZN Italia claim Noa Lang gestured towards the fans telling them to make more noise. They did not appreciate that.

Lang picks the ball up and gives it to Oliveira who puts the ball into a dangerous space. McTominay and Hojlund seem to almost get in the way of one another and the Dane’s knock-on is saved by Mandas on the goal line.

Napoli win a corner kick and send it into the box but it is dealt with well by the Lazio defence and the hosts must reset once again from the halfway line.

A bit of sustained pressure from the hosts now as they manage to work a few half chances into the Lazio box. The visitors do well to defend the opportunities but Napoli just showing a bit more intent with the ball.

Strong tackle gives Napoli the chance to break, they get the ball into the box but Lang sends a searching cross over Hojlund’s head and into empty space from the byline.

Napoli not committing the numbers into the box and it’s making it hard for them to fashion a genuine attempt on goal .

Napoli rushing things far too much when they attack, giving away possession cheaply too often and too easily. Lazio being given a lot of time on the ball whilst Napoli repeatedly turning it over.

Lazio get another good counter-attacking chance as Isaksen drives the ball forward from his own half but gets it mixed up and gives away possession.

Napoli then have a counter attack of their own before Hojlund finds himself with plenty of space and time, about 10 yards from goal, and cannot even get his attempt on target, fluffing it completely. Bit of a let off for Lazio.

Sutalo down injured after appearing to have pulled a muscle, he is receiving treatment as the Biancocelesti hurriedly prepare a substitution by the looks of things…

Lazio launch an electric counter attack this time, Noslin driving forward, before a lovely ball through for Frattesi who fires it past Milinkovic-Savic!

De Bruyne whips in the corner but Lazio get the ball clear fairly comfortably.

Napoli get a decent chance to counter-attack but they waste a lot of time in the middle of the park allowing Lazio to regroup. Lang manages to get the ball into a crossing position and fires a low one into the box but Tavares is back and deflects it out for a corner to the hosts.

#1269. Athletic Club academy trio score first senior goals in 6-1 Copa del Rey win at Prat

Three academy players scored their first goals for Athletic Club's senior side inside four minutes as Edin Terzić's team beat Prat 6-1 in the Copa del Rey. The late burst came from substitutes in a side rotated with the Basque derby in mind.

On Thursday 29 October, Athletic met Prat in the Copa del Rey round of 128. The tie was played at the Estadi La Feixa Llarga in L’Hospitalet de Llobregat. Its closing stages belonged to Athletic’s academy.

Each of the late scorers had come off the bench. Selton Sánchez finished the night with the sixth goal, teed up by Vizcay, whose own strike had started the flurry.

Aritz Conde earned an 8.2 rating from the data provider for his half-hour on the pitch. Imga, aged just 17, had made his first-team debut alongside Vizcay against Getafe the previous Sunday.

EFE reported that Athletic picked a starting XI shaped by the coming Basque derby, giving chances to players such as Yohaneko, Sannadi and Nico Serrano. Those changes did not slow the visitors.

Maroan Sannadi opened the scoring in the 29th minute. Robert Navarro doubled the lead two minutes later. Mikel Jauregizar provided both assists. Gustavo Reinke pulled one back for Prat in the 33rd minute, set up by Álex Plaza. Serrano restored the two-goal cushion three minutes later from a Jesús Areso pass.

The statistics show how one-sided the night was. Athletic had 68% of the ball and 20 shots from inside the box. They put 12 attempts on target, against 2 from the hosts. Prat’s goalkeeper was kept busy with six saves. Navarro earned the top rating of 9.2, with seven key passes in 86 minutes.

Miguel Ángel Motoso’s Prat came into the tie after beating San Rafael 5-1 and 5-0 in their two previous matches. The draw carried an echo for Athletic. Their run to their most recent Copa title began on 1 November 2023 against another Liga Élite Catalana side, about 22 km from L’Hospitalet.

#1268. Espanyol beat Villarreal 1-0 under interim Sergio García to end six-game winless run

Leandro Cabrera's goal and Ángel Fortuño's saves gave Espanyol a 1-0 win at the Estadio de la Cerámica, with B-team coach Sergio García on the touchline. The victory came three days after Manolo González was sacked and before Eder Sarabia's official presentation.

Sergio García, the B-team coach, led the side from the touchline at the Estadio de la Cerámica. The game was the opening match of the LaLiga round.

The result came three days after a change at the top. Manolo González had led the first team in 107 official matches, Libertad Digital reported. He went into that cup tie with only one point from Espanyol’s previous 15 available in LaLiga.

Villarreal controlled the ball for long spells. They completed 503 accurate passes to Espanyol’s 263. They also had 14 shots to Espanyol’s 5. Their expected goals figure was 0.92, against 0.26 for the visitors.

Espanyol thought they had taken the lead first. Roberto Fernández had a goal cancelled by VAR in the 50th minute. The review found he had held Pau Navarro before scoring. Fernández has six goals in LaLiga this season.

Cabrera then scored in the 60th minute. Bryan Zaragoza provided the assist. From there Espanyol defended their lead. Ángel Fortuño’s goalkeeping earned him the match’s top player rating of 8.31.

Villarreal had problems before half-time. Gerard Moreno went off with a muscle injury in the 17th minute and Nicolas Pépé replaced him. Foyth and Diatta had already been ruled out late. Iñigo Pérez’s side finished without a goal despite their territorial control.

The match was competitive without being dirty. Each team received three yellow cards and there were no red cards.

Espanyol named Eder Sarabia head coach on Wednesday 28 October. He could not take charge at La Cerámica because he is serving a two-match suspension, Ara reported.

Sarabia’s new staff includes former centre-back Álvaro González. He played for Espanyol from 2014 to 2017 before moving to Olympique de Marseille.

#1267. 'This club's not used to losing' - keeper Johnstone opens up on Celtic struggles

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EDT, 7 November 2026

Sam Johnstone has warned that Thursday's dramatic win over Besiktas must be seen as just the first step on Celtic's road to recovery.

The pulsating 3-2 triumph over the Turks came after Martin O'Neill's men had lost four straight matches in Europe with just three wins in the previous ten matches in all competitions.

As timely as the result was, the keeper believes there's a lot of hard work for the side to get through before anyone can talk about it being a turning point in what's been a trying season to this stage.

Asked if the spirit in the camp had been affected by a string of adverse results, Johnstone said: 'Of course it has. I think the results affect it.

'This club's not used to losing and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

'We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game.

'The lads go out to win every game, so the camp's good.

'It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people and honest with each other.

'You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result.'

Signed on loan from Wolves for the season, Johnstone was handed his chance by O'Neill only to drop out of the team following an indifferent display in the 3-0 loss at Ibrox on September 13.

Celtic goalkeeper is finding his feet in Scottish football after a difficult start

But having been selected ahead of Viljami Sinisalo in the past five matches, the former England goalkeeper believes he's steadily making progress.

'To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm,' Johnstone explained.

'It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

'I think I've got to get used to them (defenders), they've got to get used to me and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team.

'It's good. I love playing. It's a great team to play in, a great club to play for and we keep taking it game by game. We go again on Sunday.'

Johnstone moved to Celtic at the start of a difficult period which saw the side struggle for consistency.

Adamant that he's never regretted moving up to Scotland for a minute, however, he added: 'The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games.

'Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation and the lads know that.

'Like I said, we try to win every game and put things right.

Celtic fought back for a much-needed Europa League victory against Besiktas

'It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

'When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here.'

Having heard so much about Celtic Park on the night of a big European win, the keeper was glad to finally witness it for himself.

'It was unbelievable to experience this place, rocking and get the win,' he reflected.

'It's a great feeling. It's great to play in front of and feel the passion of the fans. That does help the lads and drives the lads on.

'As you could see, there were times in the game where we struggled a little bit, but the lads dug in. It's never going to be easy.

'In the Europa League, you're playing top teams and, after last week's result as well, we were under a lot of pressure. The lads came up with the goods.

'We've still got a chance to qualify, and that's our aim, so we'll take the next game the same as any other game, that we go to win.'

#1266. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

Wayne Rooney said this week that United’s players were “selfish” and “babies”. Many top players over the years have been selfish but it helped drive them and, in turn, their team to great heights, but the same cannot be said about the current bunch.

It feels at times as if it can be a long way away but it doesn’t take too much to flip the other way and we’re more than capable of doing that, I totally believe that.

Very, very good team that we’re playing again and I’m not suggesting that becomes an easy game because it doesn’t. We’ve got to respect the game, respect what it takes to win.

We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

The responsibility for me in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility, whatever goes on the pitch and what we look like, what we feel like.

Carrick had clearly thought hard about how he was going to tackle that today and what message he wanted to get across. The long and short of it was that the United manager was issuing a call to arms to his players to pull their finger out, respect the badge and start showing the kind of values of humility and hard work that the club is founded on. By name checking the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Matt Busby he was speaking about the people who exemplified the values United are all about

The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years.

I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.

No definitive answer from Carrick, who says he wants to do what is best for the football club.

There ends the broadcast section of the press conference after about 15 minutes.

Definitely a change in communication strategy from Carrick, speaking from the heart rather than waiting for questions.

My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I’m fully aware of and definitely doing something about.

I think it’s important we all recognise that. I certainly recognise it. Our supporters of are the utmost importance to me and this football club.

For them to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year and have that about us, that connection and that real vigour, intensity and enjoyment and passion is something we need to get back to.

Carrick says the dressing room is “not divided” but says it’s pretty clear the squad and everyone have to pull together and stop speaking out like has happened in public in response to questions about Martinez and Fernandes’ outbursts.

#1265. Simeone equals Luis Aragonés’s LaLiga wins record as Atlético Madrid beat Levante 2-0

Atlético Madrid won 2-0 at Levante on Saturday, making it a milestone afternoon for Diego Simeone. Barcelona are next up in the league, and one more victory would give him the coaching record on his own.

Atlético Madrid’s trip to Valencia ended with a milestone for their coach. It took the Argentine 565 LaLiga matches in charge to reach the mark, according to Club Atlético de Madrid.

The visitors went in at the interval a goal up. Álex Baena supplied the pass for their second. Earlier, Morten Hjulmand had a goal ruled out by VAR in the 17th minute. Levante coach Luís Castro was shown a yellow card for dissent a minute later.

The scoreline did not reflect the balance of chances. Levante shot 14 times from inside the box, while Atlético managed 3. The hosts’ expected goals reached 1.33, against 0.63 for the visitors.

Jan Oblak was the difference. Around the tenth minute, he made a crucial one-handed save to deny Dani Requena, Infobae (EFE) reported. The goalkeeper finished with a rating of 8.08.

Atlético had more of the ball, with 54% possession and 560 passes to Levante’s 450. Simeone made two double changes. Jonathan David and Sørloth replaced Lee Kang-In and Julián Álvarez in the 67th minute. Le Normand and Lookman came on for Barrios and Baena in the 76th.

The result was Atlético’s seventh league win in a row. It briefly took them top of the table. The teams’ last meeting, on 31 January 2026, had ended 0-0 in Valencia.

Simeone already leads Aragonés on wider measures at the club. Across all official competitions with Atlético, he has 479 wins from 813 games. Aragonés managed 308 wins from 612 games there. The club credits Simeone with eight trophies as coach, two more than Aragonés’s six.

The coming weeks carry real weight. From 11 games, Atlético have nine wins, one draw and one defeat. Real Madrid sit third on 24 points from 10 games.

By combining information from two X-ray techniques, it is possible to visualize the response of soft biological tissue to mechanical loads on multiple scales, as Newham et al.1 write in Nature. #1263. Struggling Italiano targets Anguissa for Beşiktaş

Vincenzo Italiano has identified Napoli midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa as his top January target as he tries to turn around a difficult spell at Beşiktaş.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the former Bologna and Fiorentina coach wants an experienced, physical midfielder to strengthen his side’s engine room, and the Cameroon international is at the top of his list.

Italiano took over in Istanbul in June, but Beşiktaş have won only one of their last five games. Defeats to Celtic in Europe and Trabzonspor in the league were followed by a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Kasımpaşa. Before today’s game against Gençlerbirliği, they were fifth in the Süper Lig, nine points behind leaders Galatasaray.

Anguissa turns 31 this month, and his Napoli contract expires in June 2027. Talks over a renewal have stalled, and Napoli’s poor form has weakened their position at the negotiating table.

The Partenopei have already considered selling him in January rather than losing him for nothing next summer. Inter and Atalanta have both been linked with the midfielder this season.

#1262. Furious Tottenham set to complain to authorities after Jayden Bogle escapes red card in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road

Published: 13:54 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EDT, 7 November 2026

Tottenham are to issue a formal complaint over the decision not to show a red card to Leeds defender Jayden Bogle after his challenge on Mathys Tel at Elland Road.

Video replays showed Bogle catch the Spurs forward on the back of his left ankle in the first half of Saturday’s lunchtime kick off but despite a lengthy review by the VAR, referee Jon Brooks was not sent to the pitchside monitor.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0 through a Noel Okafor goal.

Spurs, who will lodge their protest with Pro Ref, may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta in the previous Saturday’s clash at the Tottenham Stadium for his foul on Micky van de Ven.

On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a video assistant referee review.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC that the Leeds defender was ‘fortunate’ not to be dismissed.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for this foul on Micky van de Ven in the previous Saturday’s clash

‘Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent,’ Cann said. ‘He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi was more critical of his own players afterwards, but did say of the decision: 'I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

'If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.'

The decision will be reviewed by the Key Match Incidents Panel in the coming days. Mateta is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card he received in their 2–0 defeat to Tottenham.

#1261. Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty

Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2-1 at San Mamés on Sunday 1 November to end their rivals' run of four straight league wins. The visitors have formally disputed the first-half penalty that decided the derby, while Athletic lost another striker to injury.

Every goal in the Bilbao derby arrived before half-time.

Nico Williams provided the assist for the opening goal. Luka Sučić equalised on the half-hour. A crowd of 50,092 watched the game.

Before kick-off, Unai Simón presented his Yashin Trophy to the home crowd. A minute’s silence was also held for the victims of the Urda rail accident.

The visitors left Bilbao angry about the decisive spot-kick. In its official match report, Real Sociedad called it a penalty that never was and criticised VAR for not stepping in. The club statement added that the chip inside the match ball shows Jon Aramburu made contact with the ball in his challenge on Nico Williams.

Pellegrino Matarazzo said that for him it was clearly not a penalty. The Real Sociedad coach could not understand why VAR had not intervened to cancel it. He was booked for dissent in the 65th minute, a minute after Mamadou Sarr received a yellow card for the same offence. Referee Alejandro Hernandez showed Real Sociedad four yellow cards in total, against two for Athletic.

The statistics point in two directions. Real Sociedad dominated the ball, completing 514 accurate passes to Athletic’s 307. Terzić’s side created the clearer chances, however. Unai Simón made four saves, while Álex Remiro made one. Sučić was the highest-rated player on the pitch at 7.52.

The victory came at a cost. Maroan Sannadi felt his hamstring early in the game. Athletic will need one or two more days to know how long he will be out. His injury follows Gorka Guruzeta’s serious knee injury at Valencia on 17 October, which left the squad short of strikers.

With 83 minutes on the pitch, Navarro created four key passes and was rated 7.2.

The win was Athletic’s third in a row across all competitions, after a 6-1 victory over Prat and a 4-0 win against Getafe. They sit seventh, two points behind Sevilla. Real Betis are four points clear of Real Sociedad.

Athletic also have a game in hand. Their matchday-eight fixture at Rayo Vallecano was suspended. Objects landed on the field during that game, among them paper planes and tiny balls made of silicone. #1260. ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

What a strike from Nicolas Jackson to beat Gianluigi Donnarumma 😲 Villa Park erupts 🔊 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/zkuDVMevKF

Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”

When asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca said: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”

While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

Unai Emery was clear in his press conference that he sees Manchester City as one of the teams to beat this season.

We’ll have team news shortly, with Erling Haaland expected to start.

The excellent John Percy believes that Unai Emery now can claim to be the best manager in the Premier League, with few able to match his track record.

He writes: “With Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp having departed the Premier League, there can now be little doubt that Unai Emery is the best manager in England’s top division. And by some distance.

“Saturday will mark four years since Villa unveiled Emery as their head coach and few could have predicted the success that has followed. He has proved an inspired appointment who has continually embarrassed the “Big Six” clubs.

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1259. Barcelona rout Alavés 6-1 to retake LaLiga lead before top-two clash with Atlético

Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at Spotify Camp Nou to go back to the top of LaLiga. The win came with a reshuffled defence and sets up a meeting of the top two at the Metropolitano.

Atlético Madrid had gone top of LaLiga earlier on 31 October by winning at Levante. Within hours, Barcelona took the place back. Hansi Flick’s side dismantled Alavés in front of their own fans. The result ended a two-game losing run after defeats to PSG and Real Madrid.

Barcelona have scored 46 goals and conceded 12, a goal difference of +34, according to the official LaLiga table. Atlético have scored 22 and conceded 8.

This was Barcelona’s first test since the Clásico. Real Madrid won that game 2-1 at Camp Nou on 25 October. Kylian Mbappé scored twice, the second in the 87th minute, after Raphinha had equalised on 61 minutes. That defeat ended a run of nine straight league wins at the start of the season.

Raphinha opened the scoring in the 8th minute. Fermín López added a second in the 23rd. Raphinha struck again in the 41st, and Lamine Yamal made it four in first-half stoppage time. Barcelona held 77% of the ball, in front of a crowd of 53,523.

Yamal’s second goal, in the 64th minute, was first ruled out for offside. A VAR review showed his run was onside. He was taken off to a standing ovation soon afterwards, with Gordon replacing him.

The former Newcastle winger scored in the 81st minute, his first league goal for the club. He ran on to a through ball from Rodri and chipped the goalkeeper. Mariano Díaz pulled one back for Alavés in the 84th minute.

Absences left Flick short at the back. Fariñas started at right-back and played the full 90 minutes. Frenkie de Jong moved to centre-back alongside Cubarsí. João Cancelo completed the back four at left-back. Gerard Martín replaced De Jong in the 82nd minute.

Fariñas is normally a midfielder. He is from the Valencian Community and joined Barcelona as an under-14 player in 2018. He had some experience of the role, spending almost half an hour at right-back in a 2-2 pre-season draw with Birmingham City on 31 July.

¡Un #AtletiBarça por todo lo alto en #LALIGAEASPORTS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/IZy7xJkuad

Fariñas said Flick had asked whether he could play there, and that he felt nervous at first before settling into the game.

The schedule now tightens. Barcelona host Aston Villa in the fourth round of Champions League league-phase games at Spotify Camp Nou on Tuesday 3 November, kicking off at 21:00 local time.

RDaily Mail Sport's live coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Man City.

Oliver Glasner channelled his inner Jose Mourinho when Delap scored Forest's third goal, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate with his players.

In such a precarious job, this victory will mean a lot to him. There's never any guarantee of owner Evangelos Marinakis' patience.

For the first time since 2024, Manchester City have lost three consecutive games in the top fliight.

They're also just the second team in top-flight history to win their first seven games then lose the next three. The previous side to do that were Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05.

I suspect they'll beat Fulham after the international break, but you never know!

Manchester United end a day in the bottom three of the to -flight after having played at least nine games for the first time since November 1986.

Ouch. Thanks to Opta for the stat. They'll be looking to make amends against Aston Villa tomorrow but I don't back them.

Donnarumma had another poor game today, looking flappy. I'm not sure there was much he could have done about the goals, which were all worthy strikes, but conceding three goals won't help a man who has come under increasing scrutiny in recent weeks.

Here's why Maresca stood by him. Do you think it's time for a change?

Why Maresca is sticking with Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show

JACK GAUGHAN: These are tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol looked lost today. Enzo Maresca hooked the at half-time after each was at fault for one of the goals. Gvardiol was asleep, giving away the ball for the first, and Guehi just retreated as Delap ran towards goal for the second.

Well, his finishing was explosive here, as was his running and strength. He's scary when he plays like that.

Manchester United have never been in the relegation zone at this stage of a Premier League season before. Truly abysmal for them.

As for Forest, they can smile after being rewarded for their good performance. They're far from out of the woods, but they did two key things today: score at home, and get Liam Delap's confidence up. Both are critical.

Maresca straight down the tunnel and it didn’t seem as if there was a handshake between him and Oliver Glasner. Dismal night for City but the performance is in keeping with how they are playing. So susceptible on the break and when you’re making this many individual mistakes then the opponents know that they can just wait for them.

Liam Delap has been speaking to Sky Sports.

'It's been coming. We've been performing like that every week but not putting it in the net,' he said.

'We did everything right, got the three points, and are happy going into the international break.

'I just wanted to run and shoot and luckily go there and it went in the net (for first goal).

'Thankfully I put it in the net (for the second).

'We'll have to see it back (Glasner's run down the touchline). Never (seen him run like that).

'We've been deserving this for a long time. Hopefully we can build on it.'

Man City have now lost three times on the spin in the Premier League. Whatever faux title charge they were mounting is collapsing fast at this rate.

The full time whistle blows an Oliver Glasner fist pumps. A HUGE win for Nottingham Forest, one which propels them out of the relegation zone, and plunges Manchester United into it.

#1257. Serie A official line-ups: Genoa vs. Milan

Milan bring back Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric and hope to revive their fortunes against Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, who are coming off three straight wins.

It kicks off at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris at 14.00 GMT (15.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

It remains to be seen which version of Ruben Amorim’s team will turn up today, as they lurched from a 4-2 home defeat to Bologna to winning the Derby della Madonnina against Inter, to a 2-0 Europa League loss to Ferencvaros on Thursday.

In fact, they’ve won four of the last five rounds, stumbling only against Roma.

#1256. Fabián Ruiz scores twice as PSG hit Villarreal for six in record-quick start

Paris Saint-Germain scored four goals faster than any side in Champions League history on their way to a 6-0 win at La Cerámica. The defeat leaves Iñigo Pérez taking the blame and Villarreal with one win from four league-phase games.

Fabián Ruiz scored twice as Paris Saint-Germain beat Villarreal 6-0 at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Tuesday 3 November 2026. The visitors led 4-0 at the break in round four of the Champions League league stage.

João Neves opened the scoring in the ninth minute. Désiré Doué added a second three minutes later from a Maghnes Akliouche pass. Senny Mayulu struck in the 13th minute. Ruiz then converted another Akliouche assist.

That fourth goal arrived after 16 minutes and two seconds, beIN SPORTS reported. No team had ever scored four times faster in the competition. By half-time PSG had eight shots on target to Villarreal’s one.

Ruiz added his second in the 50th minute, set up by Vitinha. Flashscore described it as only the second time he had scored twice in a game for PSG. He finished with a rating of 9.81.

David Boly completed the rout in the 78th minute, with Neves providing the assist. The 17-year-old was making his Champions League debut. He scored four minutes after coming off the bench.

The numbers matched the scoreline. PSG completed 677 accurate passes to Villarreal’s 237. Their expected goals reached 2.75 against 0.74. Péter Gulácsi made six saves to keep the margin at six.

Luis Enrique managed this without four regulars. Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé, Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos all missed the trip through injury. The win was PSG’s 10th in a row. It also took them to 14 European Cup matches unbeaten, equalling the longest such run by a French club. After four matchdays, they were the only club in the league phase on 12 points.

Iñigo Pérez left Alberto Moleiro and Georges Mikautadze on the bench. He chose a less attacking line-up than usual. By the sixth goal the stadium was half empty. The fans who stayed whistled the home side again.

Pérez blamed himself for the biggest mistakes. He said his side had got their idea of how to play PSG wrong. He added that they had the wrong mindset after conceding. He also defended Carlos Macià, who had only just turned 18 and faced Vitinha. Pérez put the youngster’s struggles down to his own tactical plan.

At his press conference he would not discuss his own future. He said the squad was devastated and needed to focus on finding solutions.

Villarreal’s European campaign has stalled. They lost 3-2 at Borussia Dortmund on 8 September. A 3-1 home win over Napoli followed on 13 October. They then lost 4-3 at Liverpool on 20 October. Domestically, their previous outing was a 1-0 defeat by Espanyol.

A brilliant performance! 👏❤️💙#VCFPSG 0️⃣-6️⃣ I #UCL pic.twitter.com/6pswWcYZv5

— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_English) November 3, 2026

Spain’s other clubs had contrasting nights. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 at home. Atlético de Madrid lost 2-0 at home to Bayern München.

Villarreal return to LaLiga at home to Getafe on Sunday 8 November. Their next Champions League match is away to Slavia Praha on Wednesday 25 November, kicking off at 18:45 CET.

#1255. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

The conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

#1254. Valverde’s stoppage-time strike completes Real Madrid comeback at AEK for 12 points from 12

Substitute captain Federico Valverde struck in stoppage time as Real Madrid twice came from behind to beat AEK Athens 3-2. The win keeps Mourinho's side perfect in the league phase and takes them past his qualification target, days before a trip to Valencia without Vinícius.

Federico Valverde came off the bench in Athens and settled a match Real Madrid had trailed twice. The captain’s long-range strike arrived in the second minute of stoppage time. It completed another away comeback in this Champions League campaign. Mourinho’s side remain perfect after four matchdays.

AEK struck first. Koita put the hosts ahead in the 12th minute. Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside after a review just before the half-hour. He did not have to wait long. In the 32nd minute he equalised with a backheel from Cucurella’s cross.

AEK went ahead again with 15 minutes of normal time left. Stavros Pilios ran onto a pass from Koita and shot through Courtois’s legs. Madrid answered in less than three minutes. Denzel Dumfries played a low ball across goal and Mbappé made it 2-2.

The night ended badly for Koita. AEK’s opening scorer was sent off at 90+5, after the final whistle. He had kept protesting to the referee despite repeated warnings.

The winner carried extra weight given Valverde’s recent fitness. He felt strong discomfort in his right hamstring in the 23rd minute of the 2-1 Clásico win at Camp Nou. Mourinho said afterwards that Valverde had played more than 40 minutes injured. In Athens he started on the bench, yet still had the final say.

Madrid’s European record now reads four wins from four. They beat Inter 2-1 at home, came back to win 4-3 at Roma and beat Leipzig 4-1 at home before this trip. Their tally of 12 points takes them past the 11–12 point mark Mourinho set as the target for qualification. The next aim is a top-eight finish.

The pattern is notable. Both the Roma and AEK wins came after Madrid had fallen behind away from home. In Athens they had to respond on two separate occasions.

Attention now turns to LaLiga, where Madrid remain without Vinícius. On 16 October, the RFEF Appeals Committee rejected the club’s appeal and upheld his ban. Two games were for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair against Villarreal. The other two were for confronting the referee afterwards.
